title: GitHub - ImpossibleComputing/jacq: Jacq inference compiler and CUDA kernel DSL
excerpt: Jacq inference compiler and CUDA kernel DSL. Contribute to ImpossibleComputing/jacq development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
Jacq turns readable .jac model and kernel descriptions into CUDA. Write a model specification, inspect what the compiler understands, and generate a standalone inference runtime and weight exporter. Kernel specifications can generate standalone CUDA harnesses or supported callable library kernels.

New here? A .jac file is text, not a model checkpoint. Follow the four-lesson tutorial for a CPU-only first success and a path to GPU inference. If you already know the basics, use the five-minute quick start, format guide, or runnable examples.

First run (Rust only)

From the repository root:

cargo build -p jac-cli
./target/debug/jacq --validate examples/tinyllama.jac
./target/debug/jacq --viz examples/tinyllama.jac
./target/debug/jacq --emit-model examples/tinyllama.jac
ls generated/tinyllama/

To install the jacq command on your PATH, run cargo install --path crates/jac-cli. If you installed this checkout when the command was jac, Cargo leaves that old executable alongside jacq. Remove it with cargo uninstall --bin jac jac-cli.

You should see tinyllama_inference.cu and tinyllama_export.py. These commands need no GPU or model download. The .jac file names the Hugging Face weight source; --emit-model generates the exporter but does not run it. To compile CUDA, export weights, and generate tokens on an NVIDIA GPU, follow the next step in Quick start.

What is in this repository

  • examples/ — complete .jac model and kernel files with commands to run.
  • docs/tutorial/ — worked lessons from source text through serving evidence.
  • crates/ — parser, model IR, CUDA code generation, and the jacq CLI.
  • specs/models/ and specs/kernels/ — further model and kernel definitions.
  • integrations/vllm_kivi/ — an opt-in paged int4-KIVI integration for a pinned vLLM source checkout, with a versioned callable CUDA interface.
  • tests/ — Python tests for the vLLM integration and ABI checks.

The standalone --run path builds a generated CUDA runtime and exports weights for local inference. The vLLM setup guide covers the separate source integration for serving experiments. See ABI for its launch contract and GPU validation for a reproducible serving check.

Verification

The compiler and integration checks run on a CPU-only machine with cargo test --workspace and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v. An RTX 4090 direct-launch smoke of the emitted paged KIVI kernel passed four synthetic cases. A verified vLLM serving run on November 3, 2026 matched stock fp16 output across seven completion requests for both int4-KIVI cache writers on one 14B model. See the model-family checks for scoped standalone TinyLlama, Qwen2.5, and Mistral results and the startup compatibility follow-up for early rejection of unsupported KIVI models. See GPU validation for the repeatable procedure and current boundaries for the supported lane.

Jacq is Apache-2.0; see LICENSE and NOTICE. Contributions and local test commands are in CONTRIBUTING.md.
